title: WELCOME - Digital transition of premature and newborn infants with special care needs to post-discharge care
summary:
The WELCOME research project aims to support and strengthen parents of premature and full-term babies with increased nursing aftercare needs during the transition from acute inpatient care to the home setting. This is achieved through a new, complex digital intervention consisting of
- Synchronous intervention units (15 digital video consultations with nursing staff, as well as neonatologists and interpreters if required)
- Asynchronous components, such as digital expert consultation via chat function, teaching materials, training, individual reminders and the integration of digital technologies. 
The WELCOME intervention is an additional service to existing aftercare programmes. The ultimate goals are defined as lowering the inpatient readmission rate, reducing avoidable utilisation of emergency outpatient clinics, reducing parents' stress levels and strengthening health literacy, among other things.
conditions: Disorders related to short gestation and low birth weight, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Intervention group: In addition to usual post-discharge care, participants also receive the WELCOME tele-homecare intervention. It is based on two main components. Firstly, a synchronised, timed sequence of multilingual video consultations supported by digital assessments and homecare technologies.
Control group: The families allocated to the control group receive the standard usual post-discharge care for premature and full-term infants with increased post-discharge care needs.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Premature infants with increased socio-medical and/or nursing aftercare needs between 34-37 weeks' gestation
- Families with newborns born before the 34th week of pregnancy
- Families with newborns with extremely low birth weight (<1000g), other low birth weight (1000 to < 2500g), extreme immaturity (gestational age <28 weeks) 
- Families with sick mature infants (congenital malformations or perinatally acquired diseases) with socio-medical and/or nursing aftercare needs
Exclusion criteria:
- Families with premature infants without increased socio-medical aftercare needs or increased nursing aftercare needs
- Families with premature and full-term infants with an increased need for follow-up care in a palliative situation
